text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Designated Chancellor Viktor Klima rules out a coalition of Social Democrats with Joerg Haider's far-right Freedom Party and says he believes in the "grand coalition" of Social Democrtas and conservatives.
- Klima says he is prepared to use Freedom Party ideas for his government but will not perform free "product placement" for Haider.
- Papermaker KNP Leykam is starting talks on cutting 500 jobs in Austria.
- As mining company VA Bergtechnik is losing some powers to its Finnish parent, it has presented its employees with different restructuring models including job losses.
- Plans by Klima to shift portfolios within the government have been heavily criticised from within the Social Democratic Party.

- Labour unions want to find a replacement for Austria's higher minimum corporate tax after it was abolished by the high court. They say the government's austerity measures are no longer socially equal.
- Further mergers are expected in Austria's banking industry. However the right way has yet to be found.
- Austria' energy providers are offsetting losses with cheap imports from abroad, ahead of market liberalisation.
- The conservatives should not flirt with the Freedom Party, chancellor-designate Klima said, adding that his party intends to abide by the coalition agreement.
- GiroCredit boss Ferdinand Lacina favours closer cooperation in computing and management of Austria's banks.
- Austrian exporters do not use overseas markets well enough as they concentrate too much on Europe, the newspaper says.
